boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Bowdoin College
boards.description: An under-21-safe guide to late-night dining and study fuel near Bowdoin College, featuring on-campus traditions and local Brunswick staples with verified late hours.

cards.title: SuperSnack at Thorne Hall
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate Late-Night Tradition
cards.notes: Visit Thorne Hall for the legendary SuperSnack, featuring jalapeño poppers and grilled cheese. Available Thursday through Saturday from 10:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A beloved weekend late-night dining tradition at Bowdoin's largest dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Thorne Hall serves SuperSnack from 10:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m. on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights.
cards.access_notes: Open to students on meal plans; SuperSnack hours are 10 PM - 1 AM, Thu-Sat.

cards.title: Bowdoin Express
cards.subtitle: Smith Union's Midnight Market
cards.notes: Grab snacks, drinks, or toiletries at this lower-level Smith Union shop. It stays open until midnight every single night for all your late-night essentials.
cards.short_summary: The primary on-campus convenience store located in the basement of Smith Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Bowdoin Express is open until midnight seven days a week during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight daily; accepts Polar Points and OneCard.

cards.title: The Café at Smith Union
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Caffeine Fix
cards.notes: Head to the upper level of Smith Union for a late-night coffee or smoothie. It reopens in the evening and serves until midnight from Monday to Wednesday.
cards.short_summary: A campus cafe offering specialty coffee and smoothies with late-night weekday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Café is open from 8:00 p.m. to midnight, Monday through Wednesday.
cards.access_notes: Late hours (until midnight) apply Monday-Wednesday.

cards.title: Gelato Fiasco
cards.subtitle: Maine Street's Dessert Destination
cards.notes: Walk downtown for artisanal gelato with over 40 daily flavors. This flagship location is a student favorite and stays open until 11:00 p.m. every night.
cards.short_summary: A renowned local gelato shop offering a wide variety of flavors in a cozy downtown setting.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brunswick flagship store is open seven days a week from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11 PM daily; located within walking distance of campus.

cards.title: The Abbey
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Coffee & Community
cards.notes: Visit this unique spot for a late-night coffee or snack. It serves its full menu until 11:00 p.m. on Mondays and weekend nights, providing a quiet off-campus study vibe.
cards.short_summary: A community-focused cafe and bar that serves coffee and food late into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: The Abbey is open until 11:00 p.m. on Monday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11 PM on Mon, Fri, Sat; 10 PM on Wed-Thu.

cards.title: Taco Bell / KFC
cards.subtitle: Gurnet Road Late-Night Drive-Thru
cards.notes: For a classic fast-food run, the Taco Bell on Gurnet Road is open until midnight daily, making it a reliable choice for late-night cravings off-campus.
cards.short_summary: A standard fast-food option with a drive-thru open until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell at 17 Gurnet Road is open until 12:00 a.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell® in Brunswick, ME - 17 Gurnet Road
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until midnight daily.

cards.title: Jack Magee's Grill
cards.subtitle: Evening Burgers and Salads
cards.notes: Located in Smith Union, the Grill serves a la carte burgers and sandwiches until 8:30 p.m. most nights, serving as a primary evening dining spot for students.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus grill named after a legendary coach, offering a la carte meals in the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Jack Magee's Grill is open until 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and on Sundays.
cards.access_notes: Open until 8:30 PM Sun-Thu; accepts Polar Points and OneCard.

cards.title: Moulton Grab & Go
cards.subtitle: Quick Evening Meal Option
cards.notes: If you missed the main dinner window, Moulton Union offers a Grab & Go dinner service until 8:00 p.m. on weekdays, perfect for a quick meal between study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A convenient take-out dining option located in the historic Moulton Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Moulton Union offers Grab & Go dinner from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.
cards.access_notes: Grab & Go dinner available until 8 PM on weekdays.

cards.title: Fat Boy Drive-In
cards.subtitle: Seasonal Evening Car-Hop Service
cards.notes: Experience a 1950s-style drive-in just minutes from campus. Turn on your headlights for service and enjoy frappes and burgers until 7:00 p.m. during the season.
cards.short_summary: A historic seasonal drive-in restaurant known for its car-hop service and classic menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Fat Boy Drive-In is open until 7:00 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday during its operating season.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal operation; open until 7 PM Tue-Sat, 4 PM Sun.

cards.title: Portland Pie Company
cards.subtitle: Downtown Pizza & Pub
cards.notes: A staple for group dinners, this Maine-based chain offers gourmet pizzas with unique crusts. It serves as a reliable evening spot on Maine Street until 9:00 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A popular regional pizza restaurant offering dine-in and takeout in downtown Brunswick.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Pie Company in Brunswick is open until 9:00 p.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Open until 9 PM daily; located on Maine Street.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, specialized labs, and quiet retreats that Bowdoin students use to navigate their daily academic and social lives beyond the standard tour path.

cards.title: The Former Arctic Museum Study Space
cards.subtitle: Hubbard Hall
cards.notes: Study in the high-ceilinged space that formerly housed the Peary-MacMillan Arctic Museum; it now features modern desks and ample natural light for group or individual work.
cards.short_summary: A newly renovated reading room in the historic Hubbard Hall, repurposed from its former use as a museum space.
cards.evidence_claim: The relocation of the Peary-MacMillan Arctic Museum created a void in Hubbard Hall that is now a newly outfitted reading room available for students to study.
cards.source_title: A New Chapter: Enter the Hubbard Hall Reading Room
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; accessible to students with a valid Bowdoin ID.

cards.title: The 'Square Donut' Science Hub
cards.subtitle: Druckenmiller Hall
cards.notes: Find a seat at the tables in this sun-drenched central atrium where the historic brick of Cleaveland Hall meets the modern glass corridors of the science complex.
cards.short_summary: A spacious, light-filled atrium located at the center of the Druckenmiller Science Complex, popular for science students between labs.
cards.evidence_claim: A spacious and flexible centrally-located atrium within the Druckenmiller Science Complex is widely used as both a student study space and for department functions.
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; typically used by students in the sciences.

cards.title: The 18th-Century Parisian Lounge
cards.subtitle: Gibson Hall
cards.notes: Relax or study in this ornate lounge featuring 1730s carved oak paneling from a Parisian music salon and a collection of Renaissance instruments.
cards.short_summary: An elegant student lounge in Gibson Hall known for its historic French woodwork and quiet, classy atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gibson Salon features eighteenth-century carved oak paneling that once lined the walls of the Hôtel de Sens in Paris; students use it to study and relax.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Gibson Hall; open to students during music department hours.

cards.title: The Glass Hub for Environmentalists
cards.subtitle: Roux Center for the Environment
cards.notes: Gather in this multi-story glass atrium for community talks or find a quiet corner to study while overlooking the campus pines through floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.short_summary: A transparent, LEED-Platinum certified community space and auditorium at the heart of the Roux Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lantern is a multi-story glass circulation space and atrium-auditorium designed to be a hub for the Bowdoin community to study and attend lectures.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; often used for napping or studying between classes.

cards.title: The Quad-View 'Fishbowl'
cards.subtitle: Visual Arts Center
cards.notes: Secure a chair in this library to work while overlooking the main quad; the large windows make it a prime spot for people-watching and focused reading.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library for art history and visual arts, offering some of the best views of the Bowdoin campus quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The art library in the VAC has comfy chairs overlooking the quad and is a recommended spot for students who want a view while they work.
cards.source_title: 7 Best Study Spots for Midterm Week
cards.access_notes: Requires Bowdoin ID for entry; check library website for seasonal hours.

cards.title: The Three-Story Interior Ascent
cards.subtitle: Peter Buck Center for Health and Fitness
cards.notes: Challenge yourself on the indoor climbing wall located inside the fitness center; it spans three stories and is open for student recreational use.
cards.short_summary: A prominent indoor climbing facility located within the main campus health and wellness center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Peter Buck Center for Health and Fitness includes a three-story interior climbing wall for student use.
cards.source_title: Peter Buck Center for Health and Fitness - Facilities
cards.access_notes: Open to students during fitness center hours; equipment and orientation may be required.

cards.title: The Student Center Social Hub
cards.subtitle: David Saul Smith Union
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of the union to find pool tables, ping pong, and a space to unwind with friends between classes or in the evening.
cards.short_summary: A recreational space for students located in the main campus union, offering various games and social seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The David Saul Smith Union houses a game room, meeting rooms, and student activities offices.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; late-night hours typically align with the union's operating schedule.

cards.title: The Working Research Pier
cards.subtitle: Schiller Coastal Studies Center
cards.notes: Visit the tidal dock on Orr's Island to observe marine research in action or enjoy the views of Casco Bay from the shoreline trails.
cards.short_summary: A functional research dock and pier located at Bowdoin's coastal campus, eight miles from the main Brunswick site.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schiller campus includes a working dock where boats arrive and depart; students can walk down the dock but must not touch the boats.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; located about a 20-minute drive from the main campus.

cards.title: The Non-Academic Music Spaces
cards.subtitle: Smith Union / Sargent Gym
cards.notes: Practice with your band or solo in these rooms dedicated to non-academic musical pursuits, located within the Smith Union complex.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated practice spaces for student musicians and bands not affiliated with formal music department courses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Delta Sig Practice Rooms are available for students interested in musical practice spaces that are non-academic.
cards.access_notes: Available for student musicians; check with Student Activities for reservation procedures.

cards.title: The Screening and Media Hub
cards.subtitle: Hawthorne-Longfellow Library
cards.notes: Book a screening room for group projects or use the specialized media equipment in this tech-focused section of the main library.
cards.short_summary: A specialized area within the main library offering screening rooms and media production tools for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Media Commons includes screening rooms located in the Hawthorne-Longfellow Library available for booking.
cards.access_notes: Rooms must be reserved online; accessible during library operating hours.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Bowdoin College's campus and coastal properties through these entirely free social spaces, museums, and activities available to students and the public.

cards.title: Bowdoin College Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Walker Art Building
cards.notes: Explore over 30,000 works in a landmark building. Admission is always free for students and the public. Check out the Assyrian reliefs and the iconic rotunda murals.
cards.short_summary: A historic, free-admission art museum featuring global collections from antiquity to the present.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowdoin College Museum of Art is open to the public, and admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Visit | Bowdoin College Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. (until 8:30 p.m. on Thursdays) and Sunday 1:00 p.m.–5:00 p.m.

cards.title: Peary-MacMillan Arctic Museum
cards.subtitle: Gibbons Center for Arctic Studies
cards.notes: Visit the only museum in the lower 48 dedicated to the Arctic. See Inuit artifacts and equipment from historic polar expeditions without paying an entrance fee.
cards.short_summary: A specialized museum focused on Arctic exploration and culture with free public entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Museum is always free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Sunday 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.

cards.title: Schiller Coastal Studies Center
cards.subtitle: Orr's Island Trails
cards.notes: Hike 2.5 miles of rocky shoreline and forest trails on Orr's Island. This 118-acre coastal site is open for public use daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.short_summary: A coastal research facility with extensive hiking trails open to the public for free.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schiller campus is open for public use daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Parking is available at the trailhead kiosk.

cards.title: Harriet's Writing Room
cards.subtitle: 63 Federal Street
cards.notes: Step into the room where Stowe wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin. This historic space is open to the public for free tours on select afternoons.
cards.short_summary: A public commemorative space in the historic home where Harriet Beecher Stowe lived and wrote.
cards.evidence_claim: Harriet's Writing Room is open to the public... free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Typically open Thursdays and Fridays from 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. during the academic year.

cards.title: Hawthorne-Longfellow Library
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Library
cards.notes: Study in the historic hub named for Bowdoin's famous alumni. Visitors are welcome to use the collections and guest computers for free until 5:00 p.m. daily.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library offering free daytime access to visitors and students.
cards.evidence_claim: Visitors without library cards may use the in-house collections... there is no charge for this access.
cards.access_notes: Public access is available until 5:00 p.m. daily; after 5:00 p.m., a Bowdoin ID is required.

cards.title: Morrell Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student Union Hub
cards.notes: Relax in the central social hub of campus. This public space is ideal for people-watching, casual meetings, or attending free community-facing events.
cards.short_summary: A large, open social lounge in the student union used for studying and public events.
cards.evidence_claim: This is a public space and best for events that expect lots of foot traffic.
cards.source_title: Smith Union, Morrell Lounge for Events
cards.access_notes: Open daily during union hours; accessible to the public for general use and events.

cards.title: The Lantern
cards.subtitle: Glass Auditorium & Lounge
cards.notes: Study or attend a lecture in this LEED Platinum glass atrium. It serves as a transparent hub for environmental studies and community gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A striking glass-walled auditorium and common space designed for interdisciplinary gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lantern... is designed to be both a hub and refuge for the Bowdoin community.
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; frequently hosts free public lectures.

cards.title: Student Theater & Dance Performances
cards.subtitle: Memorial Hall
cards.notes: Catch high-quality student productions and dance concerts. Many Department of Theater and Dance shows are free and open to the public with a ticket.
cards.short_summary: Free admission to various student-led theater and dance performances throughout the year.
cards.evidence_claim: Most student shows offer free tickets through Bowdoin's ticketing site.
cards.source_title: Events | Department of Theater and Dance
cards.access_notes: Tickets are required but often free; check the online calendar for specific show dates.

cards.title: Young Artists Series Concerts
cards.subtitle: Kanbar Auditorium
cards.notes: Enjoy free classical music performances by talented festival students. These lively concerts are held in a state-of-the-art converted gymnasium.
cards.short_summary: A series of free classical music recitals featuring students from the International Music Festival.
cards.evidence_claim: All performances are free and are also livestreamed online.
cards.source_title: Young Artists Series - Bowdoin International Music Festival
cards.access_notes: Performances occur seasonally; check the festival calendar for summer and academic year dates.

cards.title: Bowdoin Pines
cards.subtitle: Old-Growth Forest Trails
cards.notes: Walk through one of the few remaining old-growth white pine stands in the region. The trails are located right next to the Roux Center and are free to access.
cards.short_summary: A historic grove of towering white pines with public walking paths adjacent to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Roux Center... let in natural light and views of the nearby pines.
cards.source_title: What Makes the Roux Center Building So Special?
cards.access_notes: Open to the public year-round for walking and nature observation.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the historic wood-paneled reading rooms of Hubbard Hall to the modern, light-filled 'Lantern' at the Roux Center, Bowdoin offers a range of environments for deep focus and collaborative work.

cards.title: Pierce Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hawthorne-Longfellow Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Find a seat in this traditional, quiet reading room. It is a central hub for focused individual study within the main library building.
cards.short_summary: A traditional quiet reading room located on the second floor of the Hawthorne-Longfellow Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pierce Reading Room is located on Level 2 of the Hawthorne-Longfellow Library and is a designated study area.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; Bowdoin ID required for entry after 5 PM.

cards.title: Hubbard Hall Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hubbard Hall, Level 1
cards.notes: Study in the former Arctic Museum space, now a bright reading room with large windows and group-friendly tables.
cards.short_summary: A newly renovated reading room in Hubbard Hall featuring ample natural light and group study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hubbard Hall Reading Room was created in the space formerly occupied by the Peary-MacMillan Arctic Museum and is available for student study.
cards.source_title: A New Chapter: Enter the Hubbard Hall Reading Room
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; features open tables and couches.

cards.title: The Lantern
cards.subtitle: Roux Center for the Environment
cards.notes: Utilize the tiered bench seating in this glass-walled auditorium for informal study with views of the campus pines.
cards.short_summary: A multi-story glass atrium in the Roux Center used for lectures and informal student study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lantern is a tiered, glassy space in the Roux Center used for informal gatherings and as a study area.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; features integrated bench seating.

cards.title: Abrahamson Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hubbard Hall, Level 6
cards.notes: Climb to the top of Hubbard Hall for a quiet, secluded study environment away from the main campus traffic.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study area located on the sixth floor of Hubbard Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Abrahamson Reading Room is located on Level 6 of Hubbard Hall and is designated as a study area.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Hubbard Hall stacks; check library hours for stack access.

cards.title: Hatch Science Library Seminar Rooms
cards.subtitle: Druckenmiller Hall
cards.notes: Book one of two mid-sized rooms equipped with whiteboards and technology for collaborative group projects.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms in the Hatch Science Library equipped with collaborative tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Hatch Science Library has two mid-sized group study rooms accommodating up to 8 people with whiteboards and projection capabilities.
cards.access_notes: Reservable online by students; available during Hatch Library hours.

cards.title: Gibson Salon
cards.subtitle: Gibson Hall
cards.notes: Study in a room featuring 18th-century French oak paneling and a marble fireplace for a sophisticated atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: An elegant student lounge in Gibson Hall known for its historic wood paneling and quiet atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gibson Salon, also known as the Gibson Lounge, features carved oak paneling and is a favorite place for students to study.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; located on the first floor of Gibson Hall.

cards.title: Beckwith Music Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Gibson Hall, Room 101
cards.notes: Use the technology-friendly furniture and listening stations in this specialized library for music-related or quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library reading room in Gibson Hall with listening equipment and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Beckwith Music Library reading room includes technology-friendly furniture and space for group study.
cards.access_notes: Open to the Bowdoin community; check specific music library hours.

cards.title: Smith Union Lounge
cards.subtitle: David Saul Smith Union
cards.notes: Choose this spot for a more social study environment near the cafe and campus mail center.
cards.short_summary: A central, active study and meeting space located within the student union.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Union serves as a primary study and meeting space for students and houses the cafe and Bowdoin Store.
cards.access_notes: Open late; typically accessible 24/7 with a Bowdoin ID.

cards.title: Edwards Center Gallery Corridors
cards.subtitle: Edwards Center for Art and Dance
cards.notes: Study surrounded by student art in the wide, bright corridors of this repurposed elementary school.
cards.short_summary: Bright, wide corridors in the Edwards Center that serve as both gallery space and informal study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Edwards Center's wide corridors are designed as gallery space and the building includes student exhibition space.
cards.source_title: Edwards Center: Adaptive Reuse at Bowdoin College
cards.access_notes: Building accessible to students; 24-hour key card access for art students.

cards.title: Media Commons Screening Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hawthorne-Longfellow Library, Basement
cards.notes: Reserve these specialized rooms for viewing media or working on digital projects in a controlled environment.
cards.short_summary: Specialized rooms in the library basement for media viewing and digital production work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Media Commons in the H-L Library basement offers reservable screening rooms and media production studios.
cards.access_notes: Reservable online; located in the basement of the main library.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the streets and corridors surrounding Bowdoin College, from the historic Federal Street district to the bustling shops of Maine Street.

cards.title: The Heart of Downtown
cards.subtitle: Maine Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk north from campus to find local favorites like Gelato Fiasco and Gulf of Maine Books in this vibrant commercial district.
cards.short_summary: Maine Street is the primary commercial corridor of Brunswick, connecting the Bowdoin campus to the town's historic downtown shops and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Maine Street and the grassy Town Mall are favorite places to shop, dine and enjoy the vibrant community.
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; business hours vary.

cards.title: Historic Federal District
cards.subtitle: Federal Street Historic District
cards.notes: View high-style Federal and Greek Revival architecture along this historic residential street bordering the north side of campus.
cards.short_summary: The Federal Street Historic District features 18th and 19th-century architecture and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.evidence_claim: The district includes a series of relatively high-style Federal and later-period houses along Federal Street and Maine Street.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; please respect private property.

cards.title: The Western Border
cards.subtitle: Park Row Corridor
cards.notes: Stroll past the Bowdoin College Museum of Art and the modern Park Row Apartments on this scenic campus-edge street.
cards.short_summary: Park Row runs along the western edge of the Bowdoin quad, housing major academic buildings and newer student apartments.
cards.evidence_claim: On the west side of the Quad along Park Row, the Mary Frances Searles Science Building (1894) houses the physics, mathematics, and computer science departments.
cards.access_notes: Public street with campus facilities; museum hours vary.

cards.title: The Route to Fat Boy
cards.subtitle: Bath Road Corridor
cards.notes: Head east on Bath Road to visit the iconic Fat Boy Drive-In, a seasonal Brunswick staple since the 1950s.
cards.short_summary: Bath Road serves as a major thoroughfare east of campus, leading to local landmarks and regional shopping.
cards.evidence_claim: Fat Boy | 111 Bath Road, Brunswick... The '50s style drive-in is a seasonal affair, with its fast food available from mid-March to mid-October.
cards.source_title: A visitor's guide to Brunswick, Maine - The Bowdoin Orient
cards.access_notes: Public road; Fat Boy is seasonal (March-October).

cards.title: The Gateway to Town
cards.subtitle: Pleasant Street Corridor
cards.notes: This busy corridor connects I-295 to downtown and features various local services and the historic Citizen building.
cards.short_summary: Pleasant Street is a primary entry point into Brunswick, hosting a mix of commercial businesses and residential conversions.
cards.evidence_claim: From I-295, take Route 1 North/Pleasant Street. Proceed to the third traffic light.
cards.access_notes: Major public thoroughfare.

cards.title: The Transit Hub
cards.subtitle: Station Avenue District
cards.notes: Catch the Amtrak Downeaster or visit the Brunswick Visitor Center located just off Maine Street on this transit-focused block.
cards.short_summary: Station Avenue is the hub for regional rail and bus travel, located steps from the Bowdoin campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brunswick Hotel is a 51-room boutique hotel conveniently located at the top of Maine Street, nestled between Bowdoin College and The Downeaster Train Station.
cards.access_notes: Public transit area; train schedules vary.

cards.title: The Riverfront District
cards.subtitle: Mill Street / Fort Andross
cards.notes: Explore the massive Fort Andross mill complex for antiques, art studios, and views of the Androscoggin River.
cards.short_summary: Mill Street leads to the historic Fort Andross complex, a repurposed textile mill that now serves as a business and arts hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Cabot Mill Antiques – is a multi-dealer antique emporium located in Fort Andross, a beautifully restored textile mill on the Androscoggin River.
cards.access_notes: Public street; mill complex open during business hours.

cards.title: Downtown Living
cards.subtitle: Union Street Corridor
cards.notes: A key residential street for off-campus students, featuring historic multi-unit apartments close to downtown amenities.
cards.short_summary: Union Street provides a mix of residential housing options for the Brunswick community and upperclassmen living off-campus.
cards.evidence_claim: 84 Union St in Brunswick is ready for you to move in. This community can be found in Brunswick on Union St.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street.

cards.title: The Community Square
cards.subtitle: Town Hall Place District
cards.notes: Located near the Town Mall, this area hosts community gatherings and is home to local eateries like Enoteca Athena.
cards.short_summary: Town Hall Place is a small connector near the Brunswick Town Mall, serving as a focal point for local dining and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Enoteca Athena... Brunswick's Italian and Greek wine bar and restaurant... located near the top of Maine Street.
cards.access_notes: Public area near the Town Mall.

cards.title: The Local Connector
cards.subtitle: Cushing Street Corridor
cards.notes: A quiet street featuring a mix of small retail spaces and residential units, just a short walk from the Maine Street action.
cards.short_summary: Cushing Street offers a quieter alternative to Maine Street with local retail and residential character.
cards.evidence_claim: 15 Cushing Street Brunswick, ME 04011 is a commercial property for lease... The property type is Retail Space.
cards.source_title: 15 Cushing Street Brunswick, ME 04011 | ID: 231768 - MyEListing
cards.access_notes: Public street with local businesses.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From signing historic books to cracking lobster claws, explore the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the Bowdoin College experience.

cards.title: Signing the Matriculation Book
cards.subtitle: A permanent mark in college history
cards.notes: Visit the President's Office during orientation to sign the historic matriculation book, joining a lineage of alumni that includes Nathaniel Hawthorne and Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.
cards.short_summary: First-year students officially join the college community by signing a historic ledger in the President's Office.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition involves first-year students visiting the president's office to sign matriculation books, a practice that has been documented with volumes dating back to the college's early history.
cards.source_title: Students Add Their Names to Bowdoin's History
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during Orientation for incoming first-year students.

cards.title: The Orientation Lobster Bake
cards.subtitle: A quintessential Maine welcome
cards.notes: Head to Farley Fields after Convocation to enjoy a traditional Maine lobster dinner with the entire campus community to kick off the academic year.
cards.short_summary: An annual outdoor feast featuring over 1,500 lobsters to welcome students back to campus in the fall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lobster Bake has opened the academic year since the 1960s and serves as a bookend tradition, with another bake held at Commencement.
cards.source_title: From sea to stomach: A peek into Lobster Bake logistics
cards.access_notes: Held on Farley Fields; open to the Bowdoin campus community.

cards.title: The Bowdoin Hello
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide culture of greeting
cards.notes: Practice the friendly habit of saying 'hello' to everyone you pass on the campus paths, a tradition rooted in 1960s fraternity culture.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing social norm where students and faculty greet one another while walking across the small campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Bowdoin Hello' is a recognized campus tradition where students greet each other on paths, originating from 1960s fraternity pledge requirements.
cards.access_notes: An informal daily practice across all campus walkways.

cards.title: Ivies Weekend
cards.subtitle: Spring's historic rite of passage
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of winter with concerts and outdoor events during this multi-day festival, which evolved from an 1865 ivy-planting ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A major spring festival featuring live music and social events, originally centered on planting ivy at the Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Ivies began as 'Ivy Day' in 1865 with the planting of ivy at the Chapel and has evolved into a weekend-long spring celebration.
cards.source_title: The Root of Ivies | Bowdoin College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in late April or early May; specific event locations vary.

cards.title: Luck of the Polar Bear
cards.subtitle: A granite mascot for good fortune
cards.notes: Visit the life-sized granite polar bear statue in front of Sargent Gym, a gift from the Class of 1912 that serves as a campus icon.
cards.short_summary: A historic granite statue of the college mascot, often visited by students for luck or photos.
cards.evidence_claim: The life-size granite polar bear statue was designed by Frederic George Richard Roth and presented to the college in 1937.
cards.source_title: The Bowdoin Bear | Peary-MacMillan Arctic Museum
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors in front of the Peter Buck Center for Health and Fitness/Sargent Gym.

cards.title: Sarah and James Bowdoin Day
cards.subtitle: Honoring academic excellence
cards.notes: Attend the fall ceremony in Pickard Theater where the top 20 percent of students are recognized as scholars and awarded historic bookplates.
cards.short_summary: An annual academic convocation that honors high-achieving students with the title of Bowdoin Scholar.
cards.evidence_claim: The ceremony recognizes the top 20 percent of students by GPA and includes the presentation of Book Awards featuring a replica college bookplate.
cards.source_title: Students Urged to Maintain an Open Mind on Sarah and James Bowdoin Day
cards.access_notes: Held annually in October in the Pickard Theater, Memorial Hall.

cards.title: Common Good Day
cards.subtitle: Service as a core value
cards.notes: Join hundreds of classmates for a day of community service in the Brunswick area, honoring President Joseph McKeen's 1802 charge.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide day of service where students, faculty, and staff volunteer at local non-profits and community sites.
cards.evidence_claim: Common Good Day is an annual event organized by the McKeen Center, rooted in the college's founding mission to serve the common good.
cards.source_title: The Joseph McKeen Center for the Common Good
cards.access_notes: Typically held on a Saturday in September.

cards.title: Winter Weekend Snow Sculptures
cards.subtitle: Icy art on the quad
cards.notes: Watch or participate in the snow sculpture competition on the quad, a tradition that has seen massive polar bears and creative designs since 1945.
cards.short_summary: A winter festival featuring snow carving, ice skating, and outdoor activities to celebrate the Maine winter.
cards.evidence_claim: Winter Weekend includes a long-standing snow sculpture tradition documented in the Orient archives since at least 1945.
cards.source_title: Buried under history: Revisiting Bowdoin's Winter's Weekend snow sculpture tradition
cards.access_notes: Held annually in February on the Main Quad.

cards.title: Dinner with Six Strangers
cards.subtitle: Breaking bread with new faces
cards.notes: Sign up for a meal hosted by faculty or staff to meet five other students you've never met, fostering community through conversation.
cards.short_summary: A residential life program that brings together small groups of students who are strangers for a shared meal.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Dinner with Six Strangers' program is a recognized tradition aimed at bringing together people on campus who may not otherwise interact.
cards.access_notes: Requires sign-up through Residential Life; locations vary by host.

cards.title: The Whispering Pines
cards.subtitle: A symbolic sprig for graduates
cards.notes: Wear a sprig of pine during the Baccalaureate ceremony, a tradition honoring the 'Whispering Pines' that have symbolized the college since 1806.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors wear pine sprigs to honor the college's historic connection to the Maine wilderness.
cards.evidence_claim: The pine tree is a central symbol of Bowdoin, with the Peucinian Society adopting the 'whispering pines' motto in 1806 and sprigs used in ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: Observed during Commencement weekend ceremonies.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Bowdoin College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to the essential first-weekend experiences for new Bowdoin students, from orientation traditions to exploring the Maine coast.

cards.title: Kick Off Arrival Day
cards.subtitle: Check-in and OneCard Pickup
cards.notes: Start your journey by picking up your OneCard and room keys at the field house before moving into your first-year brick dormitory.
cards.short_summary: The official starting point for new students to collect essentials and begin move-in.
cards.evidence_claim: Arrival Day for new students includes check-in and OneCard pickup at Farley Field House from 8:30 A.M. to 1:30 P.M.
cards.access_notes: Open to incoming students and families during scheduled orientation hours.

cards.title: Join Your Orientation Trip
cards.subtitle: Small-Group Maine Adventures
cards.notes: Bond with classmates on a device-free trip, ranging from backpacking in the mountains to community service in local towns.
cards.short_summary: A signature Bowdoin tradition involving small-group excursions across Maine to build community.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation Trips are a device-free, small-group experience designed to help new students connect and explore the Maine landscape.
cards.access_notes: Required for all first-year students; locations vary by specific trip assignment.

cards.title: Explore the Maine Coast
cards.subtitle: Harpswell Sound Research Station
cards.notes: Visit Bowdoin's 118-acre coastal campus for hiking, sailing, or watercolor painting during orientation weekend.
cards.short_summary: A coastal facility used for research and orientation trips, featuring 2.5 miles of shoreline.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schiller Coastal Studies Center hosts orientation trips involving sailing, hiking, and camping on Harpswell Sound.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via college-provided transportation during orientation or by personal vehicle.

cards.title: Dine at Thorne Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Dining Hub
cards.notes: Enjoy a meal in the largest dining hall, known for its high ceilings and views of the surrounding pine trees.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining location on campus, frequently cited for high-quality collegiate food.
cards.evidence_claim: Thorne Hall is the largest dining hall at Bowdoin and serves brunch and dinner on weekends.
cards.access_notes: Weekend brunch is served 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM; dinner 5:00 PM to 7:30 PM.

cards.title: Visit the Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Historic Walker Art Building
cards.notes: Walk through the glass pavilion to see a world-class collection ranging from ancient artifacts to modern masterpieces.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum housing over 20,000 works of art in a landmark neo-Renaissance building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowdoin College Museum of Art is open to the public and admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Open Sunday 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM; closed Mondays.

cards.title: Late Night Super Snack
cards.subtitle: Weekend Comfort Food
cards.notes: Head to Thorne Hall late at night for nachos and cookies, a favorite weekend social tradition for students.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night dining event featuring comfort food and music.
cards.evidence_claim: Super Snack occurs at Thorne Hall Thursday to Saturday nights from 10:00 PM to 1:00 AM.
cards.source_title: The insider's guide to dining at Bowdoin
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours: 10:00 PM to 1:00 AM, Thursday through Saturday.

cards.title: Practice the Bowdoin Hello
cards.subtitle: Campus Greeting Tradition
cards.notes: Adopt the friendly habit of greeting everyone you pass on the campus paths, a tradition dating back decades.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing campus culture of friendliness where students greet one another while walking.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowdoin Hello is an ongoing tradition where students greet each other on campus paths.
cards.access_notes: Occurs naturally throughout the campus at all times.

cards.title: Study in Hubbard Hall
cards.subtitle: Quiet Academic Space
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner in the historic reading room to get a head start on your first-week readings.
cards.short_summary: A grand, quiet study space located in one of the campus's most historic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hubbard Hall Reading Room is a designated quiet study space available for students.
cards.source_title: A New Chapter: Enter the Hubbard Hall Reading Room | Bowdoin College
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; check current schedule for weekend access.

cards.title: Relax at Smith Union
cards.subtitle: Student Activity Center
cards.notes: Visit the lower level for snacks at Bowdoin Express or the upper level for a smoothie at The Café.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, housing the bookstore, mail center, and multiple dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Union houses The Café, Jack Magee's Grill, and the Bowdoin Express convenience store.
cards.access_notes: Bowdoin Express is open until midnight on weekends.

cards.title: Gather at Moulton Union
cards.subtitle: Main Lounge Events
cards.notes: Check the Main Lounge for orientation events or meet up with new friends in this central campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: A historic building used for dining and various student orientation programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Moulton Union's Main Lounge is a frequent site for orientation meetings and student gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; specific event times vary by orientation schedule.
